inputs: options-flow-feed-lab.lean=call-heavy; contracts=1459; topUnusual=NVDA 227.5C $19.8M (4.6x OI); SPY 776P near put wall
items.method: Cross-read the gamma dealer regime with its flip and wall levels, the options-structure walls and front expected move, the options-flow lean and most-unusual prints, the market-heatmap breadth percentage against its 60% threshold, and the intraday session type and VWAP with the VIX band, then judge whether the positive-gamma call-led structure is confirmed or contradicted by breadth and the live tape.
items.note: Four surfaces disagree on conviction. SPY spot 776.34 sits just above the 775.35 gamma flip inside a 775/780 wall band with a tight front expected move of plus or minus 3.13, and VIX 14.25 is low and calm — a backdrop that favors a pinned, mean-reverting drift toward the walls rather than a directional break. Unusual options flow is call-heavy and leaning bullish, with 1459 contracts clearing the $250k bar inside 30 days and the top print NVDA 227.5 calls at $19.8M on 4.6x open interest, yet the third-most-unusual print is a SPY 776 put sitting right on the 775 put wall. Against that, market-heatmap breadth is narrow at 51.05% of 134 names, an -8.95-point shortfall to the 60% threshold, and the live SPY tape is a mixed, developing auction under algo control with VWAP 776.63. The positive-gamma, call-led structure therefore lacks breadth and tape confirmation this window, so a probe toward the 780 call wall above or the 775.35 flip below is better read as a range extreme to respect than a trend to chase.
items.title: Positive dealer gamma and call-led flow argue for a pin, but narrow breadth and a mixed tape withhold trend confirmation

items.method: Compare the sector rotation into and out tickers and the ETF-momentum and global-rotation leaders against the real-assets model scores and trends, flagging the sign divergence between equity leadership and hard-asset momentum.
items.note: Leadership is concentrated in equities. Sector rotation is into XLK as XLE weakens and XLV leadership fades, ETF momentum is led by tech (VGT 34.68%), and the global-rotation board is topped by ex-US names EWS (Singapore, 89/100) and EWC (Canada, 75.4) versus ACWI. The real-assets book, by contrast, is broadly soft: only industrial copper (CPER 53.3), broad commodities (DBC 49.2) and oil (USO 43.9) hold uptrends, while gold (GLD 38.2) and silver (SLV 14.1) are mixed and both bitcoin proxies (BTC-USD 32.6, IBIT 23.8) are in downtrends. The divergence reads as a risk-on equity advance rather than a reflation or hard-asset hedge bid, so real-asset vehicles are a weak diversifier and a poor confirmation source this window.
items.title: US-tech and ex-US equity leadership advances while real assets broadly trail
